the amino acids N-trimethylalanyl and N epsilon,N epsilon-tri-methyllysine can be identified and sequenced in proteins using routine methods of amino acid analysis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the methylated amino acids are not destroyed by the acid hydrolysis procedure.

the presence of methylated amino acid derivatives in proteins is easily detected by amino acid analysis and their location in the protein sequence is determined by standard sequence analysis methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of unusual amino acids can be achieved by a combination of chromatography and mass spectrometry techniques.

the use of an amino acid analyser with temperature and pH modifications to eluting buffers is the best method for the identification and determination of the location of N epsilon,Nepsilon,N epsilon-trimethylysine and N epsilon,N epsilon-di-methyllysine residues in protein sequence analysis.
